findings.title: CSRF origin comparison discards the URL scheme
findings.where: docs/plans/openshift-mvp/40-same-origin-csrf.md:95-153, especially lines 122 and 142-152; the incorrect scheme-check claim is repeated at lines 312-315, and the test matrix at lines 326-350 omits a scheme-mismatch case.
findings.what: The proposed code stores and compares `URL.host`, which contains only hostname and port. With `PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://dashboard.probaitio.com`, an Origin of `http://dashboard.probaitio.com` therefore passes even though HTTP and HTTPS are different origins. The document explicitly claims the scheme check is implicit, but `.host` excludes the scheme. This weakens the public-flavor CSRF boundary and contradicts the promised exact-origin comparison.
findings.fix: Store a canonical configured `URL.origin` and compare it with `new URL(origin).origin`. Require the hosted `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` to use `https:` and reject credentials, non-root paths, query strings, and fragments. Represent loopback development entries as explicit full origins.
findings.acceptance: A focused origin-gate test must accept the configured `https://dashboard.probaitio.com`, reject `http://dashboard.probaitio.com`, reject foreign and missing origins, preserve the intended explicit loopback origins, and fail startup for malformed or non-origin `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` values.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the proposed parser and comparator at lines 95-153, the scheme rationale at lines 312-315, and the test plan at lines 326-350 in baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. Both configured and request URLs are reduced to `.host`, conclusively erasing the scheme, and no planned assertion covers the same-host/different-scheme case.
